title: Restriction of scalars preserves and reflects local derived completeness
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal B$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal O$ any ideal sheaf. Let $\mathcal J\mathcal B$ be the ideal sheaf locally generated by images of local sections of $\mathcal J$. Use the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. An object $E\in D(\mathcal O)$ is locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete if $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],E|_U)=0$ for every object $U$ and every $f\in\mathcal J(U)$; here $\mathcal O_U$ denotes the ring sheaf on the slice site and $\mathcal O_U[1/f]$ is sheafified sectionwise localization. Use the identical definition over $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal J\mathcal B$. For every $M\in D(\mathcal B)$, restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] is locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete if and only if $M$ is locally derived $\mathcal J\mathcal B$-complete. No flatness or finite generation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 099C (lemma-restriction-derived-complete); equivalence with internal-Hom vanishing is Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af).

proof.text: For each object $U$ and section $f\in\mathcal J(U)$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-hom-tower-criterion] to identify the local derived-completeness condition over $\mathcal O$ with the vanishing of the derived multiplication tower $T(E|_U,f)$. Apply the same criterion over $\mathcal B$ to the image of $f$ and the restricted object. The vanishing-elements-ideal statement [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-complete-elements-ideal] then upgrades vanishing for these image sections to vanishing for every section of the locally generated ideal $\mathcal J\mathcal B$ (and conversely restricts the condition to the generators).

source.place: Tag 099C proof, first sentence, using Tags 0997 and 0998

proof.text: Restriction of scalars leaves the underlying sheaf of abelian groups and every multiplication-by-$f$ map unchanged: only the scalar action is precomposed with $\varphi$. By the sectionwise kernel/cokernel description of module sheaves, the cohomology sheaves of the two towers and their derived-limit vanishing are computed in the same underlying abelian-sheaf category. Therefore $T(E|_U,f)=0$ exactly when the corresponding tower over $\mathcal B_U$ is zero, proving both implications.
